To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sustainable natureculture kindergarten is a pragmatic transcorporeality of the collective engagement with present events and sustainable future events.
we need to be aware of the consequences of technology in relation to the child and the pedagogical practice.
sustainable natureculture kindergarten practice is an invitation for a transcorporeal and collective engagement with the world and a future to come.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the digital and the sustainable can be understood as part of the same process of transformation and the challenges this brings to the early childhood education and carers’ subject position.

the question of how we can use technology to support and develop sustainable natureculture praxis within early childhood education, and what kind of subject positions this implies for the kindergarten professionals.
the question of whether technology and sustainability in kindergarten can be understood as a non position.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

technology is a tool that can be used to create sustainable futures, and that the use of technology is not necessarily a problem, but rather a question of how it is implemented in the pedagogical practice.
the sustainable future requires a subject position of a non-position, which is not a position of no position.
we need to be careful not to fall in line with the technological determinism of the current society.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are not only concerned with the question of how we can make the best use of digital technologies in early childhood education and sustainable development, but we are more concerned with the question how the use of digital technologies can be used to create new forms of solidarity in early childhood education.
the future is not something that we have to prepare for, it is something that we are already in the middle of.

technology and sustainability in early childhood education and/or care are not a question of technology and sustainability per se, but rather a question of how technology and sustainability can be used to create new forms of solidarity within early childhood education.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to rethink the role of technology and technological solutions as a part of sustainable future events to be able to meet the demands of the future.
the sustainable future is not a given, but a future that we create together.
we need to rethink the subject position of sustainability in early childhood education and in relation to the digitalization of society.
